description:
So what is Carrageenan? In todays video, I talk specifically about this wonder of an ingredient. 
This is the last "off campus" video as we are moving in to our new home in 4 days!! YAY

Carrageenan is made up of 3 different types, Kappa, Iota and Lambda. All 3 different types of carrageenan do different things when combined with dairy, other stabilizers. 
If you are tring to make "low fat ice cream" , this might be one of the ingredients you are missing. When combined with Guar Gum & Locust Bean Gum, you have one of the best stabilizing combos around. 

I hope you enjoy this short video and sorry for the glancing eyes, I had to use a teleprompter due to not being able to have my notes in front of me and the camera lense is just off slightly. 

Anyway, back to "regular" filming next week and guess what.........we are unboxing the new machine and making ice cream!!! Hurrah 

As always, ask if you have any questions. 

If you enjoyed this video, please consider liking, commenting and subscribing, plus pop over to our Instagram page linked below and say hello :)

Instagram: https://tinyurl.com/2p85zcxh
Facebook: Don’t use it anymore, sorry although people still keep following!
Website: https://www.polaricecreamery.com
Ko-Fi Link: https://ko-fi.com/icecreamery


Thanks and see you on the next video :)

Hi, may i ask what type of carrageenan would you suggest for the gelato as a stabilizer? I’ve read that 4:2:1 (LBG:GG:Lcarrageenan) is the best for ice cream, but i’m not sure if it’s for gelato. Should i use kappa or ioata?

comments.author: @dandinh7136

comments.text: Yes. It’s 0.1-02% for ice cream, 0.2-0.5% for gelato. Remember you are asking the most generic question on the planet regarding the use of stabilizers, every recipe is different and I (as should everyone) balance each and every recipe individually.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: A complex subject tbh. Iota forms a soft elastic gel in the presence of dairy whereas Kappa forms a brittle gel. As Gelato doesn’t have high levels of fat I would start with Iota. As for amounts, you have the 4:2:1 and that should total 0.2-0.5% of total liquid.

comments.text:
Well the milk fat % is going to be an issue I imagine, raw milk is illegal in a lot of places so I can’t really say much about the expected fat percentage other than it’s likely between 3.5%-5%. 
I don’t know how that would react to the salep and mastic but the sugar content is fine. The main issue you have is 3% fat content in that 1000ml. You would need to create a super strong cohesive gel using stabilizers to allow it to even set. Either that, or do what other parts of the Middle East and Asia do, use starches to “set” the liquid. 
You have 27% solids which is CRAZY low too. 
You really need to create a better, balanced recipe to get this to work, uneven a little bit.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text:
@PolarIceCreamery  Thanks for the reply. About fresh milk, where I’m from here in Lebanon, and living in the mountains its totally normal to get milk from your neighborhood cow owner, and in my family we get fresh milk, pasteurize by heating. My family has made homemade yogurt and “labne” from pasteurized fresh milk since before I was born 😅.

I am kinda simmering the milk a bit having it reduce which I guess would help the fat percentage to increase a bit. 

Yesterday I did chocolate ice cream to get some left over chocolate bars used. I started with 1.1L of milk. 170g sugar + 15 grams mixed with 6 grams of salep. 100g of 55% chocolate melted (30g sugar) 68g 90% chocolate melted and 40g cacao powder. So I guess 1460g of ingredients. I weighed the whole thing after I removed from the heat and it weighed almost 1150g (maybe 50g went to my belly in the making). It also took a long time to freeze, i put the pot that was at room temperature in an iced water bowl mixed with salt at 1:30pm, 3:30pm checked on it to mix it was still almost as if I just put it, 9:45 pm the sides were barely set but still mixable with a wooden spoon. Next morning (Today) ofc it was set, I pounded it with a pestle (since im trying to follow how they pound the salep ice cream in the middle east/turkey) and moved it into a container. I liked its elasticity very nice mouthfeel with a little bite. But still dont know if that freeze time is abnormal.

Note that I’m making it at home with no pro tools or a churner. Just enjoying making ice cream and experimenting 😄

comments.text: how can I prevent my milk from curdling when I heat it up with acids?
comments.author: @김한솔-y7c

comments.text: Sometimes a little starch helps keep everything in line. Around 10g of starch mixed with 10g extra sugar would be a good place to start with before you heat the mixture too high. Also do not boil a mixture with strong acids and dairy, it’ll curdle no matter what. Warm it to 70-75c and stop there.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery
